sources.title: Self-Reorganizing Knowledge Representation for Autonomous Learning in Social Agents
sources.access: Official program p.127 author abstract; full paper not obtained; screenshot route unavailable

implemented: Authors propose CHARISMA for the CIVS artificial-life project and report experimental evaluation of SHYNE knowledge representation in a companion abstract. Exact experimental conditions and outcomes are not accessible here.
learned: Self-reorganizing knowledge structures claimed as a component result; autonomous mental development and social learning are broader proposed goals, not established outcomes.
designed: Motivational framework, context hierarchy and representation mechanism; exact initialized knowledge and selection rules remain unverified.
limit: Program abstracts do not prove completed CIVS populations, open-ended development, survival, or acquisition of underlying objectives. No exact grant traced.
ora: Direct historical overlap in ambition: artificial-life-based social learning and dynamic knowledge representation. No novelty or implementation claim follows.
rights: Publicly accessible original abstracts, institutional metadata and selected text; original synthesis only; no full documents or datasets redistributed.

sources.title: Using a Cognitive Architecture for Addressing the Question of Cognitive Universals in Cross-Cultural Psychology: The Example of Awalé
sources.access: Publisher abstract and notes; full article restricted

sources.title: Mental imagery and chunks: Empirical and computational findings
sources.access: PubMed original abstract and publisher metadata

implemented: CHREST used to model memory and game performance. 2009 author reports moderate Awalé play and approximate recall phenomena. 2008 reports human comparison involving 36 chess players and model predictions of worse recall for off-square positions.
learned: Pattern chunks from expert game examples; evidence for learned content within a designed memory system.
designed: Input domain representation, expert-level training examples, chunking mechanism, short-term capacity assumptions, task procedures.
limit: Same architecture across two games is not evidence of transfer by a single trained agent. No raw data or full method review; approximate human fit does not establish mechanistic uniqueness.
ora: Prior art for reusable learning architecture versus retained learned knowledge transferred across domains. Keep those evidentiary claims separate.
rights: Publicly accessible original abstracts, institutional metadata and selected text; original synthesis only; no full documents or datasets redistributed.

sources.title: A Context-Based Model of Attention Switching in Computer-Human Interaction Domains
Enhancing Human-computer Interaction through Use of Embedded COGNET Models
sources.access: Publisher indexed abstract and issue metadata; full paper not obtained

implemented: Human-task modeling framework combining task descriptions with shared-state control; 1991 authors describe embedding an existing model in an interface.
learned: No autonomous acquisition of domain knowledge established by reviewed abstracts.
designed: Task analysis, operator knowledge model and attention-switching infrastructure.
limit: Claimed prior validation not accompanied here by underlying results or controls. User model implemented in software is not a self-developing cognitive agent.
ora: Negative comparator for adaptive attention based on authored context rather than newly learned mechanisms.
rights: Publicly accessible original abstracts, institutional metadata and selected text; original synthesis only; no full documents or datasets redistributed.

sources.title: The Cognitive Symmetry Engine
sources.access: Institutional PDF and author-hosted copy; selected introduction, architecture section and acknowledgments; screenshots of author copy pp.1,45 failed
sources.funding: NSF grant 1021038 explicitly acknowledged in section 6, printed p.45; NSF award detail route inaccessible, recipient/amount/dates not verified

implemented: Technical reports describe component methods and a proposed integrated cognitive architecture; 2013 section 1.1 describes current architecture implementation, but complete autonomous developmental performance not established by reviewed sections.
learned: Proposed extraction of invariances from sensorimotor experience and refinement of specific representations within an innate symmetry framework; no independently established general learning outcome.
designed: Group-theoretic prior, operators, grammar and representation conventions explicitly provided. Authors describe the full integration and lifelong experience objectives as research goals.
limit: Acquiring a particular invariant does not mean inventing the abstract formalism used to encode it. Original report number discrepancy in 2012 retained. Full methods and end-to-end tests not audited.
ora: Useful distinction between acquired representation contents and pre-specified representational operators; avoid treating all prior structure as proof that learning is absent.

sources.title: CoJACK: a high-level cognitive architecture with demonstrations of moderators, variability, and implications for situation awareness
sources.access: Institutional author publication record and abstract; author manuscript excerpt dated 2012-04-29; no full method audit

implemented: Authors report modeled behavioral variability and context effects in a bounded simulation.
learned: No autonomous acquisition of the underlying cognitive architecture or objectives established by selected source.
designed: Belief/desire/intention representation, parameterized sources of variability and behavior moderators.
limit: Variation across otherwise similar agents can arise from parameter changes or noise; human-like variability does not itself establish learning or subjective experience. No operational scenario details retained. Exact funding award unresolved.
ora: Control interpretation: changing behavior over time or across individuals is not sufficient to distinguish learned information from modeled variability.
rights: Publicly accessible original abstracts, institutional metadata and selected text; original synthesis only; no full documents or datasets redistributed.
